A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FALCON, with matching authors, core algorithms, and original experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial additions and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original FALCON experiments on retrieval, VQA, and NLVR2, including ALBEF/BLIP-2 comparisons, ablations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds results for standard 4M pretraining, DataComp, SigLIP-2, and BLIP-2 Stage-2 tasks.

M1.justification: The quantile-based batch construction, Beta-distribution scheduler, and policy-gradient training remain unchanged. v4 introduces a SigLIP-2 adaptation using its generative losses as the proxy; this adaptation also replaces sigmoid contrastive loss with softmax and excludes SILC/TIPS (Sections 4.3 and 7.4).

E1.justification: v4 adds standard 4M pretraining incorporating SBU and Visual Genome captions, DataComp pretraining with its 38-task classification/retrieval evaluation suite, and BLIP-2 evaluations on OKVQA, GQA, and captioning. The original COCO/Flickr retrieval, VQA, NLVR2, and clean/noisy Conceptual Captions coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The new comparison in v4 Table 2 includes ImageBERT, UNITER, ViLT, TCL, and ALIGN, none of which had reported comparison rows in v1. Table 4 also compares SigLIP-2 with and without FALCON. The original Table 1 comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include zero-shot and fine-tuned MSCOCO retrieval under 4M pretraining, evaluation after training on a 1M CLIP/English-filtered DataComp subset, and BLIP-2 Stage-2 evaluations including CIDEr and SPICE. SigLIP-2 uses continued pretraining from an official checkpoint with modified losses. The original COCO 5K evaluation and core hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: v4 adds the learned quantile trajectory in Figure 6 and compares Conceptual Captions versus DataComp at approximately matched data budgets to examine sensitivity to the filtering model's training distribution (Section 8.4). Existing search-space, objective, and instance-level ablations, baseline sweeps, and qualitative examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v4 continues the same point-estimate reporting practice; its additional task averages do not establish uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original result entries are retained, but v4 adds substantial results in Tables 2–4 and 10–12. New 4M experiments report FALCON zero-shot text/image retrieval R@1 of 74.1/54.8. Findings are mixed: within the new SigLIP-2 comparison, FALCON changes text R@1 from 69.96 to 72.96 but image R@1 from 54.21 to 54.15; BLIP-2 captioning CIDEr is 106.0 with FALCON versus 107.2 without it.

T1.justification: v4 removes v1 Section 2's Proposition 1 and Appendix B's entire proof, including the semantic-compatibility relation, label-coverage definitions, and derivation of positive false-negative sampling probability. This eliminates the paper's formal proposition and proof; the scheduler objective and gradient-update mathematics remain unchanged.

C1.justification: v4 adds an explicit claim to be the first learning-based approach scheduling the hard/false-negative trade-off in contrastive learning and extends the abstract's named framework coverage to SigLIP-2. The central contribution remains adaptive, anchor-specific negative sampling through learned mini-batch construction.

C2.justification: v4 interprets its learned schedule as initially favoring harder negatives and subsequently reducing hardness, attributes the larger DataComp advantage to MAFA's dependence on its filtering model's pretraining distribution, and introduces an applicability limitation concerning proxies that do not involve both encoders. The earlier noisy-caption limitation remains discussed in Sections 4.1 and 8.3.

D1.justification: v4 documents SigLIP-2 checkpoint initialization and loss modifications, DataComp subset filtering, and the larger corpus composition. Core pseudocode, hardware, and hyperparameters are retained. Conversely, v1's direct BLIP dataset-download footnote and separate 567K Conceptual Captions counts are omitted.

R1.justification: v4 adds references and discussion concerning SigLIP-2, DataComp, GeoMM, additional comparison models, and large vision-language models. GeoMM is positioned as compatible but unevaluated. References supporting the deleted inevitability discussion disappear, while the principal positioning against heuristic sampling and pretrained false-negative filters remains.

P1.justification: The title changes from Vision-Language Pretraining to Vision-Language Alignment. v4 adds an explicit contribution summary, shortens the conclusion, consolidates experimental setup in the supplement, and reorders appendix material. Most existing methodological and explanatory prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout, with widespread resizing and relocation of displays. v4 adds benchmark tables and the quantile-trajectory figure, reorganizes BLIP-2 results into Stage-1/Stage-2 columns with abbreviated and full tables, and moves the clean/noisy-caption comparison from main Table 2 to supplementary Table 9.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens evidence for generality beyond v1's COCO-centered pretraining through standard 4M comparisons and DataComp's diverse evaluation suite. The SigLIP-2 and expanded BLIP-2 experiments also reveal mixed outcomes and motivate a concrete applicability boundary, improving the assessment of where FALCON helps. These gains outweigh removal of the elementary false-negative proposition, although statistical uncertainty and detailed protocols for some new evaluations remain insufficiently documented.
